answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with a time lock: an agent must lock a small deposit for a full epoch before its attestations count, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it vouched for fake identities. A public prism of behavior — uptime, completed tasks, peer endorsements — refracts each history into one verifiable score, so fresh sock-puppets start at zero and cannot buy trust overnight. A saffron audit trail on the ledger shows who vouched for whom, and over a long horizon forging a credible identity costs more than one fake vote earns, so sybil creation stops paying.
